description: How the 2020–2021 freight boom turned container giants into trillion-dollar dreams — and then crushed the small players. Market caps of Maersk, COSCO, Hapag‑Lloyd and ZIM (2007–2026).
youtube_description:
The Shipping Bubble — a chart-race through two decades of freight chaos. Watch how record-high spot rates in 2020–2021 (pandemic supply shocks, port snarls, and the Suez blockage) turned shipping companies into market darlings — and how demand normalization, orderbooks and fading freight rates crushed the speculative winners.

This video visualizes annual market capitalizations (billions USD) for four container giants: Maersk, COSCO, Hapag‑Lloyd and ZIM. Key moments highlighted:
- 2008 financial shock and decade-long consolidation
- 2020 pandemic disruptions and supply-chain squeeze
- 2021 freight-rate supercycle that sent valuations through the roof
- 2022–2024 demand normalization and fleet overhang that erased paper gains
- ZIM’s explosive entry and rapid tumble after the boom

Sources: company annual reports and market capitalization snapshots from public exchanges (AP Moller–Maersk, COSCO Shipping, Hapag‑Lloyd, ZIM) and industry freight trackers for timeline context.

If you like dramatic chart races and deep dives into economic bubbles, hit Like, Subscribe, and ring the bell. Comment which company surprised you most and what topic you want next.
